key_insight: Combining spatial and temporal information improves segmentation of time-resolved micro-CT images, helping distinguish real pore-space and fluid changes from segmentation errors.
engineering_relevance: More reliable pore geometry and fluid occupancy measurements support image-based analysis of carbon storage, hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport.
method: Apply a transformer-based 4D segmentation framework to sequential 3D images.
Use temporal context to resolve ambiguous phase assignments.
Quantify pore evolution and fluid displacement without per-image parameter adjustment.
evidence_signal: Across dissolution and fluid-displacement datasets, the framework improved pore-volume and boundary measurements over an equivalent 3D model, captured permeability increases verified against reference segmentations and flow simulations, and transferred to another dissolution sample without retraining.
watch_item: Transfer was demonstrated on another dissolution sample; robustness across broader rock types and imaging conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement
